title: Eddie Atkinson and the Chicago theaters
summary: The interviewer asks about Eddie Atkinson, who played in theaters with Dave Peyton; Jackson later took his place at the Regal Theater.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Where was Eddie Atkinson from? New Orleans. I never heard of him down here. Oh, I've seen his greatest, he's buried out by Ron Wagamahema. Did he play with bass down here? Yeah, I think so, but not in early years. In early years.
Well, I saw his picture in his family, family jazz album. Yeah, yeah. And in the uniform of brass band, you know. Yeah, the whole thing. That was a long time before he came to Chicago.
He came to Chicago in the 20s, huh?
Yeah. I'm trying to think, because.

Yeah, Eddie Atkinson is a very good musician. He played mostly in theaters, you know. He played in the Grand Theater for years. Dave Peyton, and he later on with Dave Peyton was at the Regal Theater. He played, I'd taken his place at the Regal Theater. That was before the Vitaphone, you know. We had to play the music for the pictures, fanfare, and then the stage presentation, you know.
